chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn al-Za'farani, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'The divorced woman performs Hajj during her waiting period (if her husband is pleased with the divorce).'

key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَةُ: The divorced woman (specifically one who has received a revocable or final divorce but has not yet remarried)
key_terms.طَابَتْ نَفْسُ زَوْجِهَا: Her husband was pleased (with the divorce)

ai.seo_question: When does a divorced woman perform her obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a divorced woman may perform Hajj during her 'iddah if her husband consents, highlighting the husband's authority over her marital status during this period. This ruling is particularly significant for the case of 'iddah al-talaq (divorce) where the Hajj was obligatory (Fard) while she was still married, distinguishing it from other forms of 'iddah. It underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the performance of obligatory acts during transitional marital states, provided the necessary conditions of consent and purity are met.
